_comment: P2-039 final source repair: rounded moss, three wet curled-leaf shapes, terrain-conforming wet soil and roots anchored to existing baked trees. Living canopy positions define cover islands and open clearings. Shared field shaders, terrain/control data, harvest identity, collision and actor scale are unchanged. Native matched evidence and Claude judgment remain pending.

value_lift_candidate._why_on: ON (visual lane v1/b16, 3 Nov 2026): swc storm-light set (storm_sky_1101 + soft_rain_1101 + moss_variation_1101 + value_lift_candidate) vs a fresh same-branch base (swb_base), three code-blind judges, linear slope 1.31, r 0.93, anchor RMSE 0.31: F41#5 forest ground 4.84 -> 5.84, F41#2 surge phases 5.06 -> 5.80, F41#17 6.45 -> 6.80, F41#19 5.32 -> 5.45, F41#4 5.54 -> 5.58, F41#1 4.88 -> 4.71 (noise).
value_lift_candidate._why: Owner priority 1 Nov; batch-1 judges: 'crushed near-black uniform carpet; lift values, add grove/clearing variation'. When enabled (stormwood_ground_zones.gd finish), these keys merge over this file's own: grass and moss-bush tints rise out of near-black, the terrain grass tint lightens, and the authored ground_zones field (bare loam, deep moss, still pools; r22 tuned on CPU, never GPU-judged) switches on for clearing and grove variation. Shader/tint inputs only; no bake input, collision or placement change. OFF until GPU judged.

moss_variation_1101._why_on: ON (visual lane v1/b16, 3 Nov 2026): swc storm-light set (storm_sky_1101 + soft_rain_1101 + moss_variation_1101 + value_lift_candidate) vs a fresh same-branch base (swb_base), three code-blind judges, linear slope 1.31, r 0.93, anchor RMSE 0.31: F41#5 forest ground 4.84 -> 5.84, F41#2 surge phases 5.06 -> 5.80, F41#17 6.45 -> 6.80, F41#19 5.32 -> 5.45, F41#4 5.54 -> 5.58, F41#1 4.88 -> 4.71 (noise).
moss_variation_1101._why: Cause lane tb/cause-stormwood (owner 1 Nov; judges: 'crushed near-black uniform carpet', 'player creature unreadable against the dark floor'). OFF until GPU judged; composes with value_lift_candidate (tints and ground zones). The cover-tier shader (stormwood_ground_cover.gdshader sw_*) re-hues each leaf through a broad world-space field of olive, sage and copper-brown moss while keeping its own light/dark structure, lifts the carpet's value, opens sparse clearings to the loam and pools beneath, and scatters rare wet copper and stormglass flecks that catch the storm light (the glass flecks glow faintly, natural to stormglass). Shader uniforms only: placement, bake inputs, collision and harvest identity are unchanged. No red or oxblood: the copper stays brown-orange.

ground_zones._candidate: r20 authored ground (OFF until judged). GPU F41#0 gap 1 (25 Oct, PRESENT at every outdoor Stormwood stand): one grass/moss carpet. A world-space zone field (stormwood_ground_zones.gd) turns green terrain into bare dark loam where it runs low and deep moss where it runs high; the grass tufts read the same field (grass_field.gdshader zone_*), thinning out over loam and standing short and dark in moss. Paths, rock and the Glass Sink are untouched (green ground only). Presentation only.
ground_zones._why_r21: r20 CPU judges x3 (+0.54 mapped): the loam leaned maroon (oxblood is Team Tether's) with hard decal edges, no moss read, and the opened far sheet showed a pink horizon strip. r21: cool umber loam, softer edges, flatter blue-green moss, black pools in the lowest loam, far sheet tints only. r22 (r21 judges x3: the moss read as over-saturated flat cyan, the pools as hard decals): natural dark-green moss, softer pool edges.

terrain_materials._comment: Bind installed forest-floor grain to living ground and wet earth to the muddy path, using the existing six slot IDs. Texture replacement changes presentation only; the original painted path/control maps and terrain remain authoritative.

soil._comment: Slot 1 is Terrain3D's default auto-overlay and dominates near-flat Stormwood ground. Restore the baseline forest-floor albedo/tint here; dark wet earth remains in the path, damp and canopy wet-soil layers. Normal binding stays unchanged for the isolated albedo comparison.

understory_readability._comment: The three rounded moss lobes reach 0.104m local height; canopy understory remains a separate full-height shrub tier. Harvested plants and all gameplay actors retain their own transforms.

macro_1104._why_on: ON 7 Nov 2026 (coordinator consolidation): VIS-STORMWOOD qj_macro F41#5, CPU mapped 5.31 -> 5.35. Owner 7 Nov 2026: every judged gain over what is live ships ON (a split or small gain is still a gain).
macro_1104._candidate: VIS-STORMWOOD (4 Nov 2026), F41#5 forest ground layers (5.84): judges read 'a flat green grass carpet'; qj_grass showed the carpet is the terrain wet-moss slot tiling evenly, not grass blades. Stormwood never enables Terrain3D's macro variation (Meadows does, terrain_playground.json). On: two cool moss-tone macro colours at long noise scales lay large darker and lighter drifts over the floor. Shader uniforms only; OFF until judged.

grass_patch_1104._candidate: VIS-STORMWOOD (4 Nov 2026), F41#5 forest ground layers (5.84): every judge reads the ground as 'a flat green grass carpet', 'uniform carpet', 'even scatter'. The grass shader's colony mode (clump_contrast 1.0 with a clump_patch_start/full ramp, as Tidewake dunes use) leaves true clearings below the start threshold and dense colonies above full, so the wet moss floor shows between grass colonies. Presentation only; OFF until judged.

path_loam_1104._why_on: ON (qj_path, 4 Nov 2026): CPU three-judge quick_judge A/B, calibrated slope 0.89, r 0.75, anchor RMSE 0.53: F41#4 named destinations 5.56 -> 5.92 mapped (+0.36; 3/3 prefer the darker wet path: 'sits better with the black pools', 'better value separation from the trainer'). Owner 4 Nov: a judged gain ships ON. CPU ranks only; the row closes on GPU.
path_loam_1104._candidate: VIS-STORMWOOD (4 Nov 2026), F41#4 named destinations (4.59; 'several named destinations read as similar grass and trees'): the pale sand path fills the lower half of all three close views and judges call it 'a beach texture' (also in F41#1/#5 frames). The path slot keeps its wet-earth texture but is tinted darker and cooler with deeper relief, so it reads as damp trodden forest earth. Presentation only; OFF until judged.

rock_value_1104._why: VIS-STORMWOOD (4 Nov 2026), F41#10/F41#4/F41#5: CPU judges (j4, qj_foliage) name 'a huge untextured white cliff wall' beside the Glass Sink and 'a pale white spire, blown out against the lilac sky' in the destination views; the terrain rock slot is the pale rock_scree albedo under a light #857f70 tint, and the storm sky lights it near white. On (stormwood_ground_zones.gd finish): the rock slot takes a darker cool basalt tint and deeper relief, so cliffs read as dark wet stone. Terrain material only; no geometry, collision or bake input. OFF until judged.

wet_earth_1110._why_on_1110: GPU G-stormwood-groves (10 Nov, LANE-SCOUT 5455a13d1, three code-blind judges, confirming batch): wet earth + fine rain + horizon groves together: F41#17 +0.55 (to 7.23), F41#5 +0.50, F41#4 +0.27, all 3/3; no tree-wall read. The de-pinked wet earth alone was neutral (G-stormwood-swing-2-depink).
wet_earth_1110._why: Stormwood big swing (LANE-MESHY, 10 Nov 2026; GPU judges 3/3 across F41#4/#5/#12: flat glossy black ground planes). Two sources: path_loam_1104 (ON) took the path to #6e6a5e on the dark wet_earth texture, and ground_zones (ON) paints the lowest loam as near-black (#07090b) pools at roughness 0.38. On: the path becomes a warm, banked wet-earth brown with deeper ruts (normal depth 0.75), the zone loam a lighter umber, and the pools a wet dark-brown satin instead of black gloss. No geometry, route or collision change. OFF until judged.
wet_earth_1110._why_depink: GPU stormwood-swing-1 (b85e807e1): the black gloss is gone (near-black share 0.23-0.69 -> 0.02-0.15), but under the lilac sky the warm umber loam read salmon to mauve-pink (crown_arch foreground RGB 54,46,63), too near the red reserve, and the leftover pools were hard-edged blotches. De-pinked: soil and pools are cool olive grey-brown (green >= red), and the pool band widens from [0.27, 0.335] to [0.22, 0.36] so the pool edges feather. LANE-SCOUT 1c242f1f6 (swing-1, 3/4 rows -0.23 to -0.41): the lighter warm path flattened the scene; go darker. Path back to dark olive wet earth (#6e7060: the wet_earth texture is warm umber, so the tint leans slightly green to land the albedo just red of neutral (texture mean 87,80,62; the zone shader mosses anything with green above red; CPU glass_field path R-G +10 at #74705c; #607060 tipped it green enough that the zone shader read it as grass and mossed it over), satin with deep ruts, damp slot back to its shipped #85836f, darker olive loam #2f3127 and pools #22241f. fine_rain_1110 unchanged.

pool_damp_1112._why: LANE-THINGS (12 Nov 2026), Stormwood storm states F41#22 and F41#24 (G-rescore-f41-22-24, both 6.46; 3/3: 'a flat, hard-edged grey rectangular slab at the trainer's feet in the Break frame' at giant and forest, 'flat hard-edged black pools' at giant, forest and rod_line). Both are the ground zones' pool patches: near-black with a satin sheen (roughness 0.62, specular 0.1), so they sit as black cut-outs in Calm and mirror the pale sky as a grey slab in Break. Rides last over wet_earth_1110: the pool becomes damp matte earth a step above the soil (no mirror, close in value to the loam round it), so its edge stops reading in either state. OFF until judged.

pool_satin_1104._why: VIS-STORMWOOD (4 Nov 2026), F41#5 P2-039 (CPU v1/b16 5.84, judges: 'pool specular that blows out to white in one frame'; v1/b10 3/3: 'flat lavender slabs'). In the CPU frames the value-lift black pools mirror the pale storm sky as large lilac sheets across roads and clearings. On (stormwood_ground_zones.gd config): the pools' fixed satin 0.38 roughness / 0.25 specular become 0.66 / 0.07, so they stay near-black and wet with a soft sheen. Terrain shader parameters only. OFF until judged.

_why_wet_gloss: F41#3 candidate (r11 judges: pale lilac pool slabs): the fully wet soil patches mirrored the purple sky at roughness 0.28 / specular 0.38. A duller sheen keeps them dark and wet.

forest_layers_1113._why: LANE-LAND-CS (13 Nov 2026), F41#22/#24 6.46, F41#5 6.53, F41#12 6.90, F41#2 6.19 (G-baseline-f41-22-f41-24 and G-rescore-f41-22-24, 3/3: 'black pools read as hard-edged, jagged cut-out holes'; 'a flat, hard-edged grey slab at the trainer's feet in the Break frame'). Cause, confirmed by switching it off at the forest and giant stands (CPU, same camera): the forest_layers wet_soil tier, 1,400 opaque near-black discs about 2.8 m across with an alpha-scissored ragged rim (stormwood_ground_cover.gdshader line 668). They overlap into the black cut-outs and their wet gloss mirrors the pale Break sky as the slab. The list cannot be addressed by an overlay, so this flag patches layers by name (stormwood_ground_cover.gd forest_layers()). On with layers.wet_soil.enabled false: the discs are not built; the terrain's own moss floor, soft loam zones, litter and understory show. Presentation only; no geometry, collision or route change. OFF until judged.

root_finish_1110._why_on: GPU G-f41-24-root-finish (10 Nov, LANE-SCOUT 3aaa97d83, three code-blind judges): F41#24 +0.82, 3/3; the pale canopy-root slab beside the trainer at the Fallen Giant grove is gone (a separate lilac quad, trunk dither and trainer bloom remain).
root_finish_1110._candidate: F41#24 (LANE-MESHY, 10 Nov 2026). The 'mauve quad' at the Fallen Giant grove stand is a canopy root (stormwood_ground_cover.gd _canopy_roots, drawn by the cover shader per tree, so a node pick cannot see it): a 4-facet half tube up to about 7 m long, 0.66 m wide and 0.8 m tall at the largest tree scale, which reads as a flat pale wedge. ON: rounder (8 arcs, 10 segments), thinner (width 0.13), shorter (0.7), lower (height ratio 0.8) and sunk 0.05 into the ground, with a darker wood tint. Presentation only.

fleck_round_1110._why_on: GPU G-f41-24-fleck-round (10 Nov, LANE-SCOUT 0600155b8, three code-blind judges): F41#24 +0.74, 3/3; the pale lilac notched quad beside the trainer at the Fallen Giant grove is gone (it was one glint fleck filling its whole 0.67 m cell).
fleck_round_1110._candidate: F41#24 (LANE-MESHY, 10 Nov 2026): moss_variation_1101's sw_glint fleck filled its whole floor(xz * 1.5) grid cell (0.67 m square) at roughness 0.16, specular 0.75 and stormglass-blue emission, so on a flat wet-soil patch one fleck read as a glossy lavender square reflecting the lilac sky. Each fleck is now a soft disc of sw_glint_radius_m at a jittered point inside its cell; fleck count and colours are unchanged. Presentation only.
